summary: Agent Pay is control-heavy by design: the network decides which agents may hold tokens, and the tokens carry merchant, amount and time limits. The gaps are in what happens after something goes wrong: no public way to revoke an agent or a Verifiable Intent mandate (MVCT tokens can be deleted by the integrator or suspended and cancelled by the issuer), no agent-wide kill switch, and no public agent-specific dispute rules (the Agent Pay Program Standards that Mastercard's rules require are not public).

native.note: Registered agents sign requests with RFC 9421 and the tag Agent-pay-auth; verifiers check against the Mastercard key directory at the CDN or merchant.
Registration, security review, certification and trusted agent lists; Skyfire named as Know Your Agent partner on 2026-09-30.
Consumer authorizes the agent and sets limits; passkeys in regional pilots; Verifiable Intent L2 signed by the user key.
Tokens limited by merchant, amount or time window; Verifiable Intent amount_range and budget constraints.
Merchant-specific tokens; Verifiable Intent allowed_merchants and allowed_payees; Intent API srcDpaId check.
Time-limited tokens, signature created and expires, orderExpiry, Verifiable Intent layer lifetimes (L3 at most one hour).

No public API to revoke an agent or an Agentic Token. MVCT tokens used by Agent Pay integrators can be deleted (Delete Card) and are suspended or cancelled by issuers, with notifications. Verifiable Intent 0.1 has no revocation protocol, only JWKS key removal and expiry.
Passkeys at consent; deferred orders escalated to the consumer; 3DS for agentic flows still in development at networks and EMVCo.
Mandatory nonce and short window on signatures; single-use tokens and one-time DTVC; Verifiable Intent nonce, aud and one L3 pair per mandate pair.
Verifiable Intent chain gives dispute evidence; intent records kept as chargeback evidence; no receipt object in the program.

Standard chargeback rights apply (Mastercard). No agent-specific reason code or liability rule is public: the Mastercard Rules (2026-06-02) require Agent Pay Program Standards that are not public, and Worldpay (2026-07-30) says no liability shift exists yet. Verifiable Intent leaves dispute choreography out of scope.
No public agent reputation score; the probability score rates transactions, not agents.

Mastercard aims to make agent transactions recognizable to issuers; a probability score for AI-initiated transactions is rolling out for US testing (announced 2026-09-30); Verifiable Intent risk_data at consent.
Issuers keep card-level blocks and declines; no documented control to disable one agent across the network.

gaps.title: No public revocation
gaps.description: Neither the program nor Verifiable Intent 0.1 documents how to revoke an agent or a mandate before expiry; only MVCT tokens have a documented delete and issuer suspend or cancel path.

gaps.title: No agent-wide kill switch
gaps.description: Issuers can block a card, but no documented control disables one agent across all its tokens.

gaps.title: Stateful limits without an API
gaps.description: Budgets and recurrence need the network to track spend per mandate pair; the spec defines no API for that state.

gaps.title: Dispute rules unpublished
gaps.description: No public agent-specific reason codes or liability rule as of 2026-10-21; the Mastercard Rules (2026-06-02, rules 9.2.4 and 9.5.1) require Agent Pay Program Standards, which are not public.

controlPoints.how: Certify agents and set merchant, amount and time limits when the token is provisioned.
The user signs Verifiable Intent L2 with constraints; a policy engine can review constraints before the user signs.
Verify RFC 9421 signatures, nonce and window at the CDN or merchant; block unknown keys.
Token limits, DTVC validation, Verifiable Intent constraints and cumulative budget at the network; issuer final decision.
Chargebacks under standard rules, intent records and Verifiable Intent chains as evidence, probability score for monitoring.

checklist.item: Verify agent signatures and block unknown keys
checklist.why: Mastercard's decision table blocks missing fields and unknown keys.

checklist.item: Keep a nonce cache for the signature window
Set the shortest token and mandate lifetimes that work
checklist.why: Expiry is the main revocation tool today.

checklist.item: Check intent totals and srcDpaId at Level 3
checklist.why: Mastercard says to reject totals above orderTotalAmount or a different merchant id.

checklist.item: Store intent records and Verifiable Intent chains
checklist.why: They are the evidence in a dispute.

checklist.item: If you build an agent, do not use cards on file
checklist.why: Mastercard puts this duty on agents, so the network can recognize the payment as agentic; merchants need take no action.
